title: The text editor's document
hints: Keep each undo step as "at `pos`, `removed` was replaced by `inserted`". Undo replaces `inserted` with `removed`; redo does the opposite. An insert has an empty `removed`, an erase an empty `inserted`.

For the modified flag, count steps: undo goes back one, redo forward one, a new edit forward one; the document is unmodified when that count equals the one recorded at the last save. A new edit after undoing past the save point makes the save point unreachable.
requirements: Undo and redo restore the text exactly, through any mix of inserts, erases and replacements.
Typing is grouped into words, and new lines, jumps and saves start new steps.
The modified flag follows saving, editing and undoing correctly.
Line and column conversions and find, with and without case and wrapping, behave as described.
stretch: Group consecutive Backspace presses into one step like typing, and store the caret and selection with each step so undo puts the caret back where the change happened.
